rule_name: Choose smaller YOLO variant for latency-first use
adjustment_value: Prefer nano or small variants before larger variants within the same YOLO family.
notes: Inferred from official benchmark tables where smaller variants generally have lower latency/compute; use as a suggestion rather than a hard rule.

rule_name: Choose larger YOLO variant for accuracy-first use
adjustment_value: Consider medium, large, or xlarge variants if hardware and latency budget allow.
notes: Inferred from official benchmark tables where larger variants generally have higher mAP50-95; use as a suggestion rather than a hard rule.

rule_name: Use automatic batch sizing for limited VRAM
adjustment_value: batch=-1 for automatic 60% CUDA memory utilization; alternatively batch=0.70 for 70% utilization.
notes: Ultralytics documents batch=-1 as auto mode for approximately 60% GPU memory utilization and batch=0.70 as auto mode with a specified utilization fraction.

rule_name: Use time limit when training time is constrained
adjustment_value: Set a maximum training time; time-based training can override epoch-based training.
notes: Directly supported by Ultralytics configuration documentation describing the time training argument.

rule_name: Tune hyperparameters if target metric is not met
adjustment_value: Run hyperparameter tuning with a chosen evaluation metric and tuning budget.
notes: Directly supported by Ultralytics hyperparameter tuning guide.

rule_name: Consider increasing image size for accuracy-first use
adjustment_value: Consider increasing image size if hardware allows and validation performance improves.
notes: Partly supported by image size being a configurable training/prediction parameter that affects compute; this is a tradeoff rule, not an explicit Ultralytics prescription.

rule_name: Consider reducing image size for latency-first use
adjustment_value: Consider reducing image size if latency or compute is more important than accuracy.
notes: Partly supported by image size being a configurable training/prediction parameter that affects compute and latency; this is a tradeoff rule, not an explicit Ultralytics prescription.

rule_name: Choose larger RT-DETR variants for accuracy-first use
adjustment_value: Prefer RT-DETR-R50 or RT-DETR-R101 when accuracy is prioritized and GPU memory/latency budget allow.
notes: Supported by RT-DETR benchmark tables where R50/R101 achieve higher COCO AP than smaller scaled variants.

rule_name: Use smaller RT-DETR variants or fewer decoder layers for latency-first use
adjustment_value: Prefer RT-DETR-R18/R34/R50-m or reduce RT-DETR decoder layers at inference for higher FPS without retraining.
notes: The RT-DETR paper states speed can be tuned by adjusting decoder layers without retraining and reports higher FPS for lighter/scaled variants.

rule_name: Reduce RT-DETR batch size on limited VRAM
adjustment_value: Lower per-device batch size from the reported global batch size 16 and use gradient accumulation if needed to preserve effective batch size.
notes: The paper reports global batch size 16 on four V100 GPUs; lowering per-device batch is a practical extrapolation for smaller GPUs.

rule_name: Use Objects365-pretrained RT-DETR weights for higher accuracy
adjustment_value: Prefer Objects365-pretrained weights before COCO or custom fine-tuning when available.
notes: The paper reports higher COCO AP after Objects365 pre-training followed by COCO fine-tuning for R18/R50/R101.

rule_name: Consider YOLOv10 for NMS-free low-latency detection
adjustment_value: YOLOv10
notes: Supported by YOLOv10 documentation describing NMS-free inference and latency-oriented motivation; actual speed depends on deployment hardware and export format.

rule_name: Prefer YOLO11 for stable Ultralytics deployment
adjustment_value: YOLO11
notes: YOLO11 is an official Ultralytics model family; preference for stable deployment is a recommendation-level interpretation supported by official YOLO11 documentation and YOLO12 production cautions.

rule_name: Use YOLO12 cautiously for production
adjustment_value: Community-driven model maintained primarily for benchmarking and research; possible training instability, elevated memory consumption, and slower CPU throughput.
notes: Directly supported by Ultralytics YOLO12 documentation.

rule_name: Apply full inverse-frequency class weighting for YOLO class imbalance
adjustment_value: cls_pw=1.0
notes: Ultralytics documents cls_pw=1.0 as full inverse-frequency class weighting; cls_pw=0.0 disables class weighting.

rule_name: Maximize mosaic and imgsz for tiny objects
adjustment_value: mosaic=1.0, imgsz=1280
notes: Forces network to train on artificially smaller objects without losing resolution.

rule_name: Increase weight_decay and HSV for overfitting
adjustment_value: weight_decay=0.001, higher hsv
notes: Penalizes large weights to force generalization and reduces memorization of colors.

rule_name: Increase warmup_epochs for early NaN loss
notes: Allows random initial weights to settle gently before full learning rate kicks in.

rule_name: Set close_mosaic for clean final predictions
notes: Disables heavy spatial augmentations in the final 10 epochs for clean bounding boxes.

rule_name: Heavily augment small datasets
adjustment_value: mixup=0.3, copy_paste=0.3, degrees=10.0
notes: Artificial variance is required when natural variance is missing.

rule_name: Decrease augmentation for massive datasets
adjustment_value: mosaic=0.5, mixup=0.0
notes: Prevents underfitting when natural dataset variance is already extremely high.

rule_name: Increase max_det for crowded environments
notes: Bypasses the hardcoded 300-object limit in default NMS logic.

rule_name: Linearly scale lr0 when changing batch size
adjustment_value: lr_new = lr_base * (batch_new / batch_base)
notes: Linear scaling rule for mini-batch SGD/Adam to prevent divergence.

rule_name: Enable early stopping to save compute
adjustment_value: 50 (ensure patience < epochs)
notes: Prevents wasting GPU hours on a model that has stopped improving. Standard heuristic is patience=50 when epochs=100 to 300.

rule_name: Tune RetinaNet focal loss for class imbalance
adjustment_value: Start with gamma=2 and alpha=0.25; consider gamma in 0.5-5 when imbalance severity differs.
notes: The RetinaNet paper introduces focal loss for dense-detector foreground/background imbalance and reports gamma=2 as the best practical default with robustness across a wider range.

rule_name: Scale RetinaNet batch size and LR for fewer GPUs
adjustment_value: Reference recipe is 8 GPUs x 2 images/GPU with LR 0.01 for RetinaNet; reduce per-GPU batch if needed and scale LR with effective batch/GPU count.
notes: Torchvision detection references state defaults are tuned for 8 GPUs and 2 images per GPU and provide learning-rate scaling guidance; exact lower-VRAM settings remain hardware-dependent.

rule_name: Use larger RetinaNet input scale for accuracy-first use
adjustment_value: Prefer larger image scales such as 800 when validation AP matters more than latency and GPU memory allows.
notes: The RetinaNet paper reports higher AP for larger input/backbone settings while also showing increased inference time; validate on the target dataset.

rule_name: Use smaller RetinaNet input scale for latency-first use
adjustment_value: Prefer smaller image scales such as 500 when latency or memory matters more than AP.
notes: The RetinaNet paper's speed-accuracy comparison shows smaller RetinaNet input scales have lower inference time but lower AP.

rule_name: Freeze more RetinaNet backbone layers for small datasets
adjustment_value: Use the Torchvision pretrained default of 3 trainable backbone layers or freeze more layers if overfitting appears.
notes: Torchvision documents trainable_backbone_layers with default 3 for pretrained RetinaNet; freezing more layers for tiny datasets is a conservative fine-tuning heuristic.

rule_name: Set RetinaNet class count for custom datasets
adjustment_value: <custom_num_classes>
notes: Detectron2 custom dataset docs explicitly require MODEL.RETINANET.NUM_CLASSES to match the number of thing classes; incompatible pretrained classifier layers are expected when class count changes.

rule_name: Scale Detectron2 RetinaNet LR with GPU and batch count
adjustment_value: Base config uses IMS_PER_BATCH=16 and BASE_LR=0.01 for 8-GPU training; for 1 GPU use IMS_PER_BATCH=2 and scale LR down proportionally.
notes: Detectron2 docs state configs are made for 8-GPU training and show one-GPU batch/LR scaling; Base-RetinaNet provides RetinaNet-specific IMS_PER_BATCH and BASE_LR.

rule_name: Prefer Detectron2 RetinaNet 3x schedule for accuracy-first use
adjustment_value: Use 3x schedule MAX_ITER=270000 with STEPS=210000|250000 instead of 1x MAX_ITER=90000 when compute allows.
notes: Detectron2 RetinaNet model zoo reports higher R50 AP for the 3x schedule than the 1x schedule; official configs define the 1x and 3x iteration schedules.

rule_name: Increase Detectron2 detections per image for crowded scenes
adjustment_value: Set above 100 when test images may contain more than 100 objects.
notes: Detectron2 custom dataset docs state TEST.DETECTIONS_PER_IMAGE controls the maximum objects detected and should be increased for images with more than 100 objects.

rule_name: Replace Faster R-CNN predictor for custom classes
adjustment_value: Use FastRCNNPredictor(in_features, num_classes) after loading COCO-pretrained fasterrcnn_resnet50_fpn weights.
notes: Torchvision finetuning tutorial explicitly shows replacing the pretrained FastRCNNPredictor head for the target class count.

rule_name: Set Faster R-CNN ROI class count for custom datasets
adjustment_value: <custom_num_classes>
notes: Detectron2 custom dataset docs require MODEL.ROI_HEADS.NUM_CLASSES to match the number of thing classes; incompatible pretrained classifier layers are expected when class count changes.

rule_name: Scale Faster R-CNN batch size and LR for fewer GPUs
adjustment_value: Torchvision reference defaults are 8 GPUs x 2 images/GPU with LR 0.02; Detectron2 Base-RCNN-FPN uses IMS_PER_BATCH=16 and BASE_LR=0.02. Scale LR with effective batch size when reducing GPUs.
notes: Torchvision train script states defaults are tuned for 8 GPUs and 2 images per GPU and gives LR scaling guidance; Detectron2 docs also show one-GPU batch/LR scaling.

rule_name: Prefer Faster R-CNN 3x schedule for accuracy-first use
adjustment_value: Use 3x schedule MAX_ITER=270000 with STEPS=210000|250000 instead of 1x MAX_ITER=90000 when compute allows.
notes: Detectron2 model zoo reports higher R50-FPN AP for the 3x schedule than the 1x schedule; official configs define 1x and 3x iteration schedules.

rule_name: Increase Faster R-CNN detections per image for crowded scenes
adjustment_value: Set above 100 when test images may contain more than 100 objects.
notes: Detectron2 custom dataset docs state TEST.DETECTIONS_PER_IMAGE controls the maximum objects detected and should be increased for images with more than 100 objects.

rule_name: Freeze more Faster R-CNN backbone layers for small datasets
adjustment_value: Use the Torchvision pretrained default of 3 trainable backbone layers or freeze more layers if overfitting appears.
notes: Torchvision documents trainable_backbone_layers with default 3 for pretrained Faster R-CNN; freezing more layers for tiny datasets is a conservative fine-tuning heuristic.

rule_name: Keep or raise Faster R-CNN RPN proposals for recall-sensitive tasks
adjustment_value: Keep the Detectron2 default POST_NMS_TOPK_TEST=1000 for Faster R-CNN FPN and validate before reducing proposal counts.
notes: Detectron2 Base-RCNN-FPN config sets RPN pre/post-NMS proposal counts; reducing proposals is an accuracy-latency tradeoff that should be validated on the target dataset.

rule_name: Use SSD backbone weights for custom class counts
adjustment_value: For custom class counts, initialize SSD300 with num_classes=<custom_num_classes> and weights_backbone=VGG16_Weights.IMAGENET1K_FEATURES; do not assume weights=DEFAULT can directly fine-tune a different class count.
notes: Torchvision SSD docs expose num_classes and weights_backbone; source code overrides num_classes to COCO categories when COCO detector weights are used.

rule_name: Reduce SSD batch size on limited VRAM
adjustment_value: Reference SSD300 recipe uses batch-size 4 per GPU on 8 GPUs; reduce per-GPU batch if memory is limited and retune learning rate if effective batch changes.
notes: Torchvision SSD300 reference command gives batch-size 4 and LR 0.002 on 8 GPUs; exact LR scaling for changed SSD effective batch is not explicitly prescribed.

rule_name: Use SSD-specific augmentation policy
adjustment_value: Use data_augmentation=ssd as the starting augmentation policy for SSD300 training.
notes: Torchvision SSD300 reference command uses --data-augmentation ssd; the preset applies photometric distort, zoom-out, IoU crop, and horizontal flip.

rule_name: Keep SSD300 fixed input size unless changing architecture
adjustment_value: Use 300x300 input for SSD300 VGG16; choose another SSD variant rather than freely changing image size.
notes: Torchvision SSD300 docs state images are resized to a fixed size and the source constructs SSD300 with fixed size (300, 300).

rule_name: Freeze more SSD backbone layers for small datasets
adjustment_value: Use the Torchvision pretrained default of 4 trainable backbone layers or freeze more layers if overfitting appears.
notes: Torchvision documents trainable_backbone_layers with default 4 for pretrained SSD300; freezing more layers for tiny datasets is a conservative fine-tuning heuristic.

rule_name: Tune SSD NMS threshold for duplicate detections
adjustment_value: Start from the Torchvision SSD default nms_thresh=0.45 and decrease if duplicate boxes persist after validation.
notes: Torchvision SSD source code sets nms_thresh=0.45; lowering NMS threshold is a post-processing tradeoff that should be validated on the target dataset.

rule_name: Tune SSD score threshold for false positives
adjustment_value: Start from the Torchvision SSD default score_thresh=0.01 and raise it if false positives are too frequent.
notes: Torchvision SSD source code sets score_thresh=0.01; score-threshold tuning is a validation-time precision-recall tradeoff.

rule_name: Replace ResNet50 final classifier for custom classes
adjustment_value: Use nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, <custom_num_classes>) after loading ResNet50 pretrained weights.
notes: PyTorch transfer-learning tutorial shows replacing the final fully connected layer for the target class count; applies directly to ResNet50 because TorchVision exposes the same fc classifier structure.

rule_name: Freeze ResNet50 backbone for very small datasets
adjustment_value: Set backbone parameters requires_grad=False and train only model.fc as a fixed feature extractor.
notes: Official tutorial describes fixed-feature extraction as freezing all layers except the final layer; recommended as a conservative starting point for small custom datasets.

rule_name: Fine-tune all ResNet50 layers for domain shift
adjustment_value: Use full fine-tuning from ImageNet pretrained weights instead of feature extraction when the target domain differs substantially and enough labeled data exists.
notes: Official tutorial describes full fine-tuning as initializing from ImageNet pretrained weights and training the rest as usual; validate to avoid overfitting.

rule_name: Scale ResNet50 learning rate when changing batch size or GPU count
adjustment_value: Reference ResNet recipe uses 8 GPUs with batch_size=32 per GPU and LR=0.1; scale LR with effective batch size when changing GPU count or batch size.
notes: Torchvision classification reference notes learning-rate scaling when using a different number of GPUs or batch size.

rule_name: Prefer Torchvision ResNet50 V2 recipe for accuracy-first ImageNet pretraining
adjustment_value: Use torchvision_resnet50_imagenet_v2_training when training ResNet50 from scratch for ImageNet-style accuracy and compute budget allows 600 epochs.
notes: TorchVision docs and PyTorch blog report 80.858 top-1 for IMAGENET1K_V2 versus 76.13 for IMAGENET1K_V1.

rule_name: Use the matching ResNet50 pretrained-weights transforms
adjustment_value: Use weights.transforms(): IMAGENET1K_V2 uses resize=232 and crop=224; IMAGENET1K_V1 uses resize=256 and crop=224 with ImageNet normalization.
notes: TorchVision documents the preprocessing transforms stored with each ResNet50 weight enum; mismatched preprocessing can invalidate benchmark comparisons.

rule_name: Replace MobileNetV3 final classifier for custom classes
adjustment_value: Use nn.Linear(model.classifier[3].in_features, <custom_num_classes>) after loading MobileNetV3 pretrained weights.
notes: PyTorch transfer-learning tutorial supports replacing the final classifier for custom classes; TorchVision MobileNetV3 source shows the final classifier layer is classifier[3].

rule_name: Freeze MobileNetV3 features for very small datasets
adjustment_value: Set backbone/features parameters requires_grad=False and train only the classifier head.
notes: Official transfer-learning tutorial describes fixed feature extraction by freezing all layers except the final layer; adapt to MobileNetV3 by freezing features and training classifier[3].

rule_name: Scale MobileNetV3 learning rate when changing batch size or GPU count
adjustment_value: Reference MobileNetV3 V1 recipe uses 8 GPUs with batch_size=128 per GPU and LR=0.064; scale/retune LR when changing effective batch size or GPU count.
notes: TorchVision classification reference provides the MobileNetV3 8-GPU recipe. Its LR-scaling guidance appears elsewhere in the same reference rather than as a MobileNetV3-specific statement; treat this as a practical heuristic and validate.

rule_name: Prefer MobileNetV3 Large V2 recipe for accuracy-first use
adjustment_value: Use torchvision_mobilenetv3_large_imagenet_v2_training for MobileNetV3 Large ImageNet-style training when compute budget allows 600 epochs.
notes: TorchVision docs and issue 3995 report higher MobileNetV3 Large V2 top-1/top-5 than V1, using regularization tuning.

rule_name: Use matching MobileNetV3 pretrained-weights transforms
adjustment_value: Use weights.transforms(): MobileNetV3 Large V2 uses resize=232 and crop=224; V1 Large/Small use resize=256 and crop=224 with ImageNet normalization.
notes: TorchVision documents preprocessing transforms stored with each MobileNetV3 weight enum; mismatched preprocessing can invalidate benchmark comparisons.

rule_name: Train only MobileNetV3 classifier head for small ImageNet-like datasets
adjustment_value: True; train classifier[3] first and keep features frozen unless validation underfits.
notes: CS231n states exact phrase: not a good idea to fine-tune the ConvNet due to overfitting concerns. Surgical fine-tuning also warns that tuning more parameters on a small target dataset can forget pretraining information.

rule_name: Validate partial or full MobileNetV3 unfreezing under domain shift
adjustment_value: Compare head-only against unfreezing later blocks or all features with a lower backbone LR.
notes: Yosinski et al. state exact phrase: transferability of features decreases as the distance between the base task and target task increases. Surgical fine-tuning finds shift type influences which subset to tune.

rule_name: Tune MobileNetV3 fine-tuning LR by dataset and domain similarity
adjustment_value: Do not reuse ImageNet pretraining LR; search smaller backbone LR such as 1e-5 to 1e-4 and classifier LR such as 1e-4 to 1e-3.
notes: Li et al. state exact phrase: dataset dependent but also sensitive to the similarity between the source domain and target domain. Use validation to choose LR/momentum.

rule_name: Use broader MobileNetV3 tuning when dataset is large and dissimilar
adjustment_value: False; initialize from pretrained weights but fine-tune through the feature extractor with conservative LR.
notes: CS231n states exact phrase: enough data and confidence to fine-tune through the entire network. Yosinski et al. support that distant transfer can still beat random features.

rule_name: Replace EfficientNet final classifier for custom classes
adjustment_value: Use nn.Linear(model.classifier[1].in_features, <custom_num_classes>) after loading EfficientNet pretrained weights.
notes: PyTorch transfer-learning tutorial supports replacing the final classifier for custom classes; TorchVision EfficientNet models use classifier[1] as the final Linear layer.

rule_name: Freeze EfficientNet features for very small datasets
adjustment_value: Set feature extractor parameters requires_grad=False and train only classifier[1] first.
notes: Official transfer-learning tutorial describes fixed feature extraction by freezing all layers except the final layer; adapt to EfficientNet by freezing features and training classifier[1].

rule_name: Use matching EfficientNet pretrained-weights transforms
adjustment_value: Use weights.transforms(); TorchVision EfficientNet B0-B7 crop sizes are 224, 240, 288, 300, 380, 456, 528, and 600 respectively, with ImageNet normalization.
notes: TorchVision documents preprocessing transforms stored with each EfficientNet weight enum; mismatched resize/crop settings can invalidate benchmark comparisons.

rule_name: Prefer smaller EfficientNet variants under limited VRAM
adjustment_value: Start with EfficientNet-B0/B1/B2 or reduce batch size before using B4-B7; larger variants require higher crop sizes and much higher GFLOPs.
notes: TorchVision EfficientNet metadata shows crop size and GFLOPs rise from B0 to B7; validate accuracy/latency tradeoff on target hardware.

rule_name: Validate partial or full EfficientNet unfreezing under domain shift
adjustment_value: Compare head-only against unfreezing later blocks or all features with a lower backbone LR.
notes: Yosinski et al. show transferability decreases as source/target task distance grows; surgical fine-tuning finds shift type influences which subset to tune.

rule_name: Tune EfficientNet fine-tuning LR by dataset and domain similarity
adjustment_value: Do not reuse ImageNet pretraining LR; search smaller backbone LR such as 1e-5 to 1e-4 and classifier LR such as 1e-4 to 1e-3.
notes: Li et al. show fine-tuning hyperparameters are dataset-dependent and sensitive to source/target domain similarity; choose LR/momentum by validation.

rule_name: Use documented RandAugment settings for large EfficientNet variants
adjustment_value: For EfficientNet-B5 use augment_name=randaugment; randaug_num_layers=2; randaug_magnitude=17. For EfficientNet-B7 use augment_name=randaugment; randaug_num_layers=2; randaug_magnitude=28.
notes: Official TensorFlow TPU EfficientNet README gives exact RandAugment options for EfficientNet-B5 and B7/B8 checkpoints.

rule_name: Replace ViT-B-16 final classifier for custom classes
adjustment_value: Use nn.Linear(model.heads.head.in_features, <custom_num_classes>) after loading ViT-B-16 pretrained weights.
notes: PyTorch transfer-learning tutorial supports replacing the final classifier for custom classes; TorchVision VisionTransformer source shows the final classifier is heads.head.

rule_name: Freeze ViT-B-16 encoder for very small datasets
adjustment_value: Freeze patch projection and encoder parameters and train only heads.head first.
notes: Official transfer-learning tutorial describes fixed feature extraction by freezing all layers except the final layer; adapt to ViT-B-16 by training only heads.head as a conservative starting point.

rule_name: Use matching ViT-B-16 pretrained-weights transforms
adjustment_value: Use weights.transforms(): IMAGENET1K_V1 uses crop=224; SWAG_E2E uses resize=384 and crop=384 with bicubic interpolation.
notes: TorchVision documents preprocessing transforms stored with each ViT-B-16 weight enum; mismatched preprocessing can invalidate benchmark comparisons.

rule_name: Interpolate ViT-B-16 positional embeddings when changing resolution
adjustment_value: Use TorchVision interpolate_embeddings with reset_heads=True when loading pretrained ViT-B-16 weights at a different image size.
notes: TorchVision Vision Transformer source provides interpolate_embeddings for applying pretrained checkpoints to different image resolutions and supports resetting classifier heads.

rule_name: Prefer 224px ViT-B-16 or reduce batch under limited VRAM
adjustment_value: Prefer 224px IMAGENET1K_V1 transforms or lower batch size before SWAG_E2E 384px fine-tuning; attention/FLOPs rise substantially at 384px.
notes: TorchVision metadata reports ViT-B-16 GFLOPs of 17.564 at 224px and 55.484 at 384px for SWAG_E2E.

rule_name: Tune ViT-B-16 fine-tuning LR by dataset and domain similarity
adjustment_value: Do not reuse the 0.003 ImageNet pretraining LR directly; search smaller backbone LR such as 1e-5 to 1e-4 and classifier LR such as 1e-4 to 1e-3.
notes: Li et al. show fine-tuning hyperparameters are dataset-dependent and sensitive to source/target domain similarity; TorchVision ViT-B-16 pretraining recipe uses AdamW with substantial regularization that should be retuned for custom data.

rule_name: Consider SWAG E2E ViT-B-16 weights for accuracy-first transfer
adjustment_value: Prefer ViT_B_16_Weights.IMAGENET1K_SWAG_E2E_V1 when 384px inference/fine-tuning cost and license constraints are acceptable.
notes: TorchVision and SWAG sources report higher ImageNet-1K top-1 for SWAG_E2E than IMAGENET1K_V1 but at larger 384px resolution and higher GFLOPs.

rule_name: Use CLIP normalization for CLIP fine-tuning and inference
adjustment_value: Use bicubic resize/center crop and CLIP mean=0.48145466|0.4578275|0.40821073 std=0.26862954|0.26130258|0.27577711; in FT-CLIP set clip_mean_and_std=true.
notes: OpenAI CLIP source defines these preprocessing statistics; FT-CLIP explicitly enables CLIP mean/std for ImageNet-1K fine-tuning.

rule_name: Use layer-wise LR decay for CLIP fine-tuning
adjustment_value: For CLIP ViT-B/16 ImageNet-style fine-tuning start with layer_decay=0.6 and lower learning rates in earlier visual layers.
notes: FT-CLIP identifies layer-wise learning-rate decay as important for keeping lower-layer CLIP representations from changing too much; the official config uses 0.6 for CLIP-Base/16.

rule_name: Use FT-CLIP effective batch size for recipe reproduction
adjustment_value: batch_size=256 per GPU on 8 GPUs with update_freq=1 for effective batch size 2048.
notes: FT-CLIP repository states the CLIP-Base/16 command uses batch_size 256 per GPU and effective batch size equals GPUs times batch size times update frequency.

rule_name: Disable MixUp CutMix and drop path for FT-CLIP-style fine-tuning
adjustment_value: mixup=0; cutmix=0; drop_path=0.
notes: FT-CLIP reports MixUp and CutMix as disabled in the final config and finds increasing drop path hurts fine-tuning performance.

rule_name: Use FT-CLIP regularization defaults for ImageNet-style fine-tuning
adjustment_value: RandAug m9 n2 mstd0.5; label_smoothing=0.1; random_erase=0.25 pixel; model_ema_decay=0.9998.
notes: FT-CLIP final config reports RandAug, label smoothing 0.1, random erase 0.25, and EMA 0.9998 for CLIP-Base/16 fine-tuning.

rule_name: Reduce CLIP batch size before changing core fine-tuning recipe on limited VRAM
adjustment_value: Start by reducing per-GPU batch size below 256 or using gradient accumulation; keep 224px before trying larger 384px CLIP-B/16 fine-tuning.
notes: FT-CLIP recipe is documented for 8x A100-40GB with per-GPU batch 256; the same source reports CLIP-B/16 384px requires 55.4G FLOPs versus 17.5G at 224px.

rule_name: Replace Swin V2 classifier head for custom classes
adjustment_value: Use nn.Linear(model.head.in_features, <custom_num_classes>) after loading Swin V2 pretrained weights.
notes: TorchVision SwinTransformer source defines the final classification layer as model.head; use the same transfer-learning head replacement pattern as other TorchVision classifiers.

rule_name: Use matching Swin V2 pretrained-weights transforms
adjustment_value: Use weights.transforms(): Swin V2 T/S resize=260 crop=256; Swin V2 B resize=272 crop=256 with bicubic interpolation and ImageNet normalization.
notes: TorchVision documents per-weight Swin V2 preprocessing transforms; mismatched resize/crop can invalidate benchmark comparisons.

rule_name: Match Swin V2 window transfer when fine-tuning at higher resolution
adjustment_value: For Microsoft SwinV2-B* 22K-to-1K use 192->256 with window 12->16 or 192->384 with window 12->24 and pretrained_window_sizes=12|12|12|6.
notes: Swin V2 paper motivates log-spaced continuous position bias for transferring low-resolution pretrained models to high-resolution inputs; Microsoft configs give exact 256px and 384px window-transfer settings.

rule_name: Use checkpointing and gradient accumulation for Swin V2 under limited VRAM
adjustment_value: Use --accumulation-steps and --use-checkpoint before reducing model size; Swin get-started notes checkpointing can save about 60 percent memory for Swin-B.
notes: Microsoft Swin get-started guide recommends gradient accumulation and checkpointing when GPU memory is insufficient and gives Swin-B memory-saving guidance.

rule_name: Use TorchVision Swin V2 regularization defaults for ImageNet-style training
adjustment_value: label_smoothing=0.1; mixup_alpha=0.8; cutmix_alpha=1.0; random_erase=0.25; auto_augment=ta_wide.
notes: TorchVision SwinTransformer V2 reference recipe reports these regularization settings for Swin V2 T/S/B ImageNet-1K training.

rule_name: Consider Microsoft 22K-pretrained 384px SwinV2-B* for accuracy-first use
adjustment_value: Use microsoft_swinv2_b_22kto1k_384_finetune when ImageNet-style accuracy matters and 384px compute budget is acceptable.
notes: Microsoft Swin model hub reports SwinV2-B* 384px fine-tuning at 87.1 top-1 versus 86.2 top-1 at 256px and higher FLOPs.

rule_name: Use DINOv2 processor transforms for fine-tuning and inference
adjustment_value: Use AutoImageProcessor/DINOv2 preprocessor settings: resize shortest_edge=256, center_crop=224, rescale, RGB conversion, and ImageNet mean/std normalization.
notes: DINOv2 processor config and Transformers docs define preprocessing; mismatched transforms can invalidate image-classification comparisons.

rule_name: Set DINOv2 classifier for custom labels
adjustment_value: Load with AutoModelForImageClassification.from_pretrained(..., num_labels=<custom_num_classes>, id2label=..., label2id=...) so the image-classification head matches the dataset.
notes: Transformers image-classification guide uses AutoModelForImageClassification with explicit num_labels/id2label/label2id; DINOv2 docs state the classifier is a linear layer on the CLS token.

rule_name: Prefer frozen DINOv2 features on very small datasets
adjustment_value: Freeze the DINOv2 backbone and train a linear head first; unfreeze later only if validation data supports it.
notes: Meta reports strong DINOv2 features with classifiers as simple as linear layers and publishes official frozen linear-evaluation heads; this is a safer starting point for tiny datasets.

rule_name: Reduce DINOv2 memory pressure by variant choice or accumulation
adjustment_value: Prefer ViT-S/14 or ViT-B/14 before ViT-L/14 or ViT-g/14; reduce per-device batch and use gradient accumulation for Trainer fine-tuning.
notes: Official parameter counts range from 21M to 1100M and the Transformers fine-tuning guide uses gradient_accumulation_steps=4 with per-device batch 16.

rule_name: Disable unused-column removal for DINOv2 Trainer fine-tuning
adjustment_value: remove_unused_columns=False
notes: Transformers image-classification fine-tuning guide sets remove_unused_columns=False so custom image transform columns are preserved for Trainer batching.

rule_name: Consider larger DINOv2 variants for accuracy-first frozen-feature classification
adjustment_value: Prefer ViT-L/14 or ViT-g/14 when memory allows; DINOv2 with registers can improve official linear top-1 but is tracked separately from the base no-register variants.
notes: Meta's official table reports higher linear-evaluation accuracy for larger DINOv2 variants and includes even stronger register variants in the same model hub.

rule_name: Disable YOLO augmentations for label-sensitive validation runs
affected_field: hsv_h, hsv_s, hsv_v, translate, scale, fliplr, mosaic, erasing, auto_augment
adjustment_value: hsv_h=0.0; hsv_s=0.0; hsv_v=0.0; translate=0.0; scale=0.0; fliplr=0.0; mosaic=0.0; erasing=0.0; auto_augment=None
notes: Ultralytics provides this exact no-augmentation training example with disabled values.

rule_name: Set YOLO HSV augmentation for outdoor lighting variation
adjustment_value: hsv_h=0.03; hsv_s=0.6; hsv_v=0.5
notes: Ultralytics shows this exact custom augmentation example and describes HSV shifts as useful for outdoor/lighting and camera variation.

rule_name: Use 10-degree YOLO rotation augmentation for orientation variation
adjustment_value: degrees=10.0
notes: Ultralytics documents degrees=10.0 as an exact example that samples rotations between -10.0 and 10.0 degrees and states rotation is crucial when objects appear at different orientations.

rule_name: Use YOLO scale=0.5 for object distance and size variation
adjustment_value: scale=0.5
notes: Ultralytics documents scale=0.5 as the default and states it samples final scale factors from 0.5 to 1.5 to handle objects at different distances and sizes.

rule_name: Use YOLO CutMix probability 0.5 for occlusion-heavy scenes
adjustment_value: cutmix=0.5
notes: Ultralytics documents cutmix=0.5 as an exact example and states CutMix helps recognize objects when partially occluded by other objects.

rule_name: Disable YOLO mosaic for the final 20 epochs of a 200-epoch run
adjustment_value: mosaic=1.0; epochs=200; close_mosaic=20
notes: Ultralytics states that with epochs=200 and close_mosaic=20 mosaic is disabled after 180 epochs; mosaic=1.0 means the transform is always applied before close_mosaic disables it.

rule_name: Set YOLO single-class training for object-presence-only datasets
adjustment_value: single_cls=True
notes: Ultralytics documents single_cls as treating all classes in multi-class datasets as a single class during training.

rule_name: Set YOLO rectangular batching for efficiency on varied aspect ratios
adjustment_value: rect=True
notes: Ultralytics documents rect=True as minimum padding to a common size and states it can improve efficiency and speed but may affect accuracy.

rule_name: Set YOLO multi-scale training to +/-25 percent
adjustment_value: multi_scale=0.25
notes: Ultralytics documents multi_scale=0.25 as varying image size from 0.75x to 1.25x each batch.

rule_name: Set YOLO inference batch above 1 for offline directory inference
adjustment_value: batch=<largest_value_that_fits_memory>; default batch=1
notes: Ultralytics documents inference batch default 1 and states larger batch size can provide higher throughput for directory/video/list sources.

rule_name: Set YOLO stream_buffer=False for real-time video
adjustment_value: stream_buffer=False
notes: Ultralytics documents stream_buffer=False as dropping old frames to accommodate new frames and being optimized for real-time applications.

rule_name: Set YOLO augment=True for robustness-first prediction
adjustment_value: augment=True
notes: Ultralytics documents augment=True as test-time augmentation that can improve detection robustness at the cost of inference speed.

rule_name: Use the official RT-DETR multi-scale training list
notes: Official RT-DETR PyTorch config defines this exact multi_scale list for the R50 config.

rule_name: Use 10x lower RT-DETR backbone learning rate
adjustment_value: backbone_lr=0.00001; lr=0.0001
notes: Official RT-DETR optimizer config sets params matching backbone to lr=0.00001 and the main optimizer lr to 0.0001.

rule_name: Use official RT-DETR dataloader batch sizes for recipe reproduction
adjustment_value: train_dataloader.batch_size=4; val_dataloader.batch_size=8
notes: Official RT-DETR dataloader config sets train batch_size=4 and validation batch_size=8.

rule_name: Use Detectron2 documented one-GPU batch/LR settings
adjustment_value: SOLVER.IMS_PER_BATCH=2; SOLVER.BASE_LR=0.0025
notes: Detectron2 getting-started docs state configs are made for 8-GPU training and give this exact one-GPU example.

rule_name: Set Detectron2 detections per image to expected object maximum
adjustment_value: TEST.DETECTIONS_PER_IMAGE=<expected_max_objects_per_image>; must be >100 for images with more than 100 objects
notes: Detectron2 custom-dataset docs state TEST.DETECTIONS_PER_IMAGE controls the maximum number of objects and should be set larger if test images may contain >100 objects.

rule_name: Preserve LLaVA global batch when changing GPU count
adjustment_value: Keep per_device_train_batch_size * gradient_accumulation_steps * num_gpus equal to the reference global batch size: 256 for pretraining and 128 for visual instruction tuning.
notes: Official LLaVA training docs state that when training on fewer GPUs users should reduce per-device batch size and increase gradient accumulation while keeping global batch size unchanged.

rule_name: Use LoRA for lower-memory LLaVA fine-tuning
adjustment_value: Use official LoRA fine-tuning with lora_r=128, lora_alpha=256, learning_rate=2e-4, and mm_projector_lr=2e-5 before attempting full-model 13B fine-tuning on limited VRAM.
notes: Official LLaVA repository recommends LoRA when GPU memory is insufficient and reports fitting 13B training on 8 A100-40GB or 8 RTX A6000 and 7B training on 8 RTX3090.

rule_name: Use 4-bit or 8-bit LLaVA inference under low VRAM
adjustment_value: Use --load-4bit or --load-8bit for model_worker or CLI inference; validate accuracy because quantization may reduce quality.
notes: Official LLaVA repository documents 4-bit/8-bit inference and notes reduced memory footprint with potential accuracy impact.

rule_name: Pad non-square images for LLaVA-1.5 instruction tuning
adjustment_value: image_aspect_ratio=pad
notes: Official LLaVA training notes say padding non-square images to square instead of cropping slightly reduces hallucination.

rule_name: Group LLaVA batches by modality for mixed instruction data
adjustment_value: group_by_modality_length=True
notes: Official LLaVA docs recommend this only when instruction tuning data contains both language-only and multimodal examples and report about 25 percent speedup without affecting the final outcome.

rule_name: Add explicit short-answer format prompts for VQA data
adjustment_value: Append: Answer the question using a single word or phrase.
notes: LLaVA-1.5 paper identifies ambiguous answer-format prompts as a key multitask-balancing issue and uses explicit response-format prompts for VQAv2 GQA TextVQA MME and POPE evaluation/training examples.

rule_name: Increase LLaVA input resolution for detail-heavy VQA when memory allows
adjustment_value: Use CLIP ViT-L/14 336px for LLaVA-1.5; consider HD grid-style higher-resolution processing for OCR or fine-detail tasks if memory and context budget allow.
notes: LLaVA-1.5 improves over the original by scaling to 336px and LLaVA-1.5-HD improves detail-heavy benchmarks by splitting higher-resolution images into grids with global context.

rule_name: Use lower LLaVA pretraining LR with MLP projector
adjustment_value: learning_rate=1e-3 for LLaVA-1.5 MLP projector pretraining
notes: LLaVA-1.5 paper states the pretraining learning rate is halved due to the MLP projection layer instead of the original linear projection layer.

rule_name: Enable FlashAttention for Qwen VL memory pressure
adjustment_value: flash_attention_2
notes: Official Qwen2.5-VL model card recommends FlashAttention 2 for better acceleration and memory saving especially in multi-image and video scenarios; Qwen VL fine-tuning notes also mention adding flash_attention_2 to config.json.

rule_name: Tune Qwen VL min_pixels and max_pixels for visual-token budget
adjustment_value: Use lower max_pixels for memory/latency; raise max_pixels for OCR, documents, and fine-detail VQA when validation improves. Model-card example token range is 256-1280 visual tokens; fine-tuning example uses min_pixels=16*28*28 and max_pixels=576*28*28.
notes: Official Qwen2.5-VL model card states the default visual-token range is 4-16384 and min_pixels/max_pixels can be set to balance performance and cost; Qwen VL fine-tuning README says training resolution is critical.

rule_name: Use very low learning rate for Qwen VL fine-tuning
adjustment_value: Start with 2e-7 and search from 1e-6 down to 2e-7.
notes: Official Qwen VL fine-tuning README states the suggested learning rate is from 1e-6 to 2e-7 and the example script uses 2e-7.

rule_name: Freeze Qwen VL vision tower when training with image and video data
adjustment_value: False
notes: Official Qwen VL fine-tuning README states that if trained with both image and video data tune_mm_vision should be False.

rule_name: Reduce Qwen3.6 context length only when OOM requires it
adjustment_value: Default native context is 262144; reduce if OOM occurs, but keep at least 128K when possible to preserve thinking capabilities.
notes: Official Qwen3.6 model card recommends reducing context on OOM but maintaining at least 128K tokens where possible.

rule_name: Use 8-way tensor parallel serving for Qwen3.6 full context
notes: Official Qwen3.6 model card gives SGLang and vLLM serving commands with tensor-parallel size 8 for 262144-token context.

rule_name: Avoid ZeRO-3 for Qwen3-VL MoE fine-tuning
adjustment_value: Do not use DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 for Qwen3-VL MoE models; validate alternative distributed training support.
notes: Official Qwen VL fine-tuning README states Qwen3VL MoE does not support DeepSpeed with ZeRO-3 and load-balancing loss is not supported in the Hugging Face implementation at that time.

rule_name: Prefer real-time detectors for autonomous-driving street scenes
adjustment_value: YOLOv10|YOLO11|RT-DETR
notes: BDD100K and Cityscapes establish street/autonomous-driving imagery as diverse urban perception data; YOLO and RT-DETR model evidence should be used to choose the exact latency/accuracy tradeoff.

rule_name: Use driving-domain datasets for street-scene model selection
adjustment_value: bdd_100k|cityscapes
notes: BDD100K and Cityscapes are direct representative datasets for driving and urban street-scene perception.

rule_name: Let performance and hardware dominate for general everyday objects
adjustment_value: Use task metric performance hardware and user constraints before domain-specific overrides.
notes: COCO and ImageNet establish broad common-object and visual-recognition settings; this domain is intentionally generic rather than specialized.

rule_name: Prefer efficient video-friendly detectors for traffic surveillance
adjustment_value: YOLOv10|YOLO11
notes: UA-DETRAC establishes real-world traffic video detection and tracking as the domain context; YOLO evidence should be used to select a speed-oriented detector variant.

rule_name: Consider stronger detectors for offline traffic surveillance analysis
adjustment_value: RT-DETR|Faster R-CNN
notes: UA-DETRAC establishes vehicle detection/tracking in traffic surveillance; RT-DETR and Faster R-CNN evidence support higher-accuracy detector options when real-time latency is not the primary constraint.

rule_name: Prefer stronger transfer-learning classifiers for fine-grained wildlife and nature
adjustment_value: SwinV2|ViT-B-16|DINOv2|EfficientNet
notes: iNaturalist and CUB establish visually similar species and fine-grained categories as core domain properties; model-family evidence should be used to choose capacity under hardware limits.

rule_name: Account for imbalance and low-shot classes in wildlife nature datasets
adjustment_value: ClassImbalance|LowShotClasses
notes: iNaturalist directly reports long-tail class imbalance varied image quality and poor performance on classes with small numbers of training examples.

rule_name: Prefer fine-grained-capable classifiers for vehicle make-model recognition
adjustment_value: SwinV2|ViT-B-16|DINOv2|EfficientNet
notes: Stanford Cars and fine-grained vehicle evaluation evidence establish make-model-year recognition with subtle visual differences; choose architecture capacity according to hardware and data size.

rule_name: Use efficient classifiers for clean e-commerce catalog images
adjustment_value: EfficientNet|MobileNetV3|ResNet
notes: DeepFashion2 establishes retail fashion recognition tasks while EfficientNet MobileNetV3 and ResNet evidence support practical classifier choices with different efficiency/accuracy tradeoffs.

rule_name: Prefer dense-scene detectors for retail shelf or cluttered product scenes
adjustment_value: YOLO11|RT-DETR|Faster R-CNN
notes: DeepFashion2 documents real-world clothing-item annotations with scale viewpoint and occlusion variation; detector-family evidence supports choosing speed or accuracy according to deployment constraints.

rule_name: Prefer OCR or VQA framing for handwritten document reading tasks
adjustment_value: visual_question_answering
notes: IAM establishes offline handwritten text recognition as document/text recognition data; Qwen VL evidence supports document/OCR-capable VLM use when the requested output is reading or answering document questions.

rule_name: Avoid label-changing geometry augmentations for handwritten digits and text
adjustment_value: large_rotation|vertical_flip|unconstrained_horizontal_flip
notes: MNIST and IAM establish handwritten characters/text as recognition targets where character orientation and shape encode labels; use conservative geometry transforms only when validation confirms invariance.
